question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Simple Interest percentage is the product of rate and time.

⇒ Total SI% = 7% × 6 = 42%

⇒ Simple Interest = 42% of ₹3500

⇒ Simple Interest = (42 ÷ 100) × 3500 = 1470

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1470.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Effective SI% = 7% × 6 = 42%

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹3500

Rate (R) = 7% per annum

Time (T) = 6 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (3500 × 7 × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 3500 × 42 ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 35 × 42

⇒ SI = 1470

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1470.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount paid or received is the sum of Principal and Simple Interest: Amount = P [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Compound Interest (CI)

Unlike SI, CI is calculated on the principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods. Formula: CI = P[(1 + R ÷ 100)T − 1].

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

For the same principal and rate of interest, the difference between CI and SI for exactly 2 years is directly calculated as: D = P(R ÷ 100)².
